label: Backpressure
limitations: This custom lane is intentionally smaller than general software-engineering and language worlds.
statement: Backpressure slows or rejects producers when downstream capacity is exhausted rather than hiding unbounded growth.

label: Bounded queue
limitations: This custom lane is intentionally smaller than general software-engineering and language worlds.
statement: A bounded queue limits admitted work and makes overload behavior explicit.

label: Typed event bus
limitations: This custom lane is intentionally smaller than general software-engineering and language worlds.
statement: A typed bus transports declared messages while preserving message identity and delivery errors.

label: Cancellation
limitations: This custom lane is intentionally smaller than general software-engineering and language worlds.
statement: Cancellation is an explicit state transition whose safety depends on what work can be interrupted and what cleanup is guaranteed.

label: Cancellation-safety control
limitations: This custom lane is intentionally smaller than general software-engineering and language worlds.
statement: Dropping an arbitrary future must not be assumed safe without checking its partial-effect behavior.

label: Capability boundary
limitations: This custom lane is intentionally smaller than general software-engineering and language worlds.
statement: A capability grants a narrow operation on an explicit resource and does not imply adjacent authority.

label: Capability expansion control
limitations: This custom lane is intentionally smaller than general software-engineering and language worlds.
statement: Permission for one operation must not silently authorize neighboring resources or actions.

label: Typed command
limitations: This custom lane is intentionally smaller than general software-engineering and language worlds.
statement: A command requests an operation and carries the data and identity required to decide it.

label: Rust compiler boundary
limitations: This custom lane is intentionally smaller than general software-engineering and language worlds.
statement: The Rust compiler validates types, ownership, lifetimes, and declared trait contracts but cannot prove application requirements or runtime environment behavior.

label: Compiler-is-not-completion control
limitations: This custom lane is intentionally smaller than general software-engineering and language worlds.
statement: A clean compile must not be reported as proof that requirements, integration, or user behavior are correct.

label: Correlation identifier
limitations: This custom lane is intentionally smaller than general software-engineering and language worlds.
statement: A correlation identifier links commands, events, logs, and results belonging to one logical operation.

label: Duplicate-delivery control
limitations: This custom lane is intentionally smaller than general software-engineering and language worlds.
statement: At-least-once delivery must not be treated as exactly-once execution without an idempotency mechanism.

label: End-to-end proof
limitations: This custom lane is intentionally smaller than general software-engineering and language worlds.
statement: An end-to-end proof exercises the user-visible path through the real orchestrator, workers, boundaries, and result surface.

label: Typed event
limitations: This custom lane is intentionally smaller than general software-engineering and language worlds.
statement: An event records an accepted state transition or observed outcome in a form downstream components can interpret without string guessing.

label: Bounded worker pipeline
limitations: This custom lane is intentionally smaller than general software-engineering and language worlds.
statement: A typed command enters a bounded channel, one state owner validates the transition, a worker returns a correlated event, and overload is rejected before unbounded allocation.

label: Cancellation-safe ownership
limitations: This custom lane is intentionally smaller than general software-engineering and language worlds.
statement: An orchestrator cancels a child task only after the resource owner defines how partially completed I/O, locks, buffers, and completion events are reconciled.

label: End-to-end host boundary
limitations: This custom lane is intentionally smaller than general software-engineering and language worlds.
statement: A Rust coordinator passes a typed request through the real process boundary, verifies the returned identity and receipt, and distinguishes that proof from an in-memory mock.

label: Idempotent retry and reconciliation
limitations: This custom lane is intentionally smaller than general software-engineering and language worlds.
statement: A timed-out effect retains its operation identity; a bounded retry is allowed only after the worker can deduplicate it, and reconciliation determines whether the original attempt committed.

label: Failure isolation
limitations: This custom lane is intentionally smaller than general software-engineering and language worlds.
statement: Failure isolation prevents one component fault from corrupting unrelated state or authority.

label: Mock-only boundary control
limitations: This custom lane is intentionally smaller than general software-engineering and language worlds.
statement: A mocked integration must not be reported as an operational host-boundary proof.

label: Idempotency key
limitations: This custom lane is intentionally smaller than general software-engineering and language worlds.
statement: An idempotency key lets repeated delivery identify an already accepted logical operation.

label: Integration test
limitations: This custom lane is intentionally smaller than general software-engineering and language worlds.
statement: An integration test verifies operational boundaries among real components and transports.

label: Application invariant
limitations: This custom lane is intentionally smaller than general software-engineering and language worlds.
statement: An invariant is a condition that must remain true across every permitted state transition.

label: Secret-observability control
limitations: This custom lane is intentionally smaller than general software-engineering and language worlds.
statement: Observability must not expose credentials, private payloads, or secret material.

label: Observability
limitations: This custom lane is intentionally smaller than general software-engineering and language worlds.
statement: Logs, metrics, and traces expose state transitions, queue pressure, latency, failures, and causal identifiers without exposing secrets.

label: Orchestrator
limitations: This custom lane is intentionally smaller than general software-engineering and language worlds.
statement: An orchestrator coordinates state and work ownership without absorbing every component's domain logic.

label: Orchestrator monolith control
limitations: This custom lane is intentionally smaller than general software-engineering and language worlds.
statement: Coordination does not authorize the orchestrator to absorb every worker's domain logic and storage.

label: Single state owner
limitations: This custom lane is intentionally smaller than general software-engineering and language worlds.
statement: Mutable orchestration state has an explicit owner so concurrent components cannot silently create competing truth.

label: Operation provenance
limitations: This custom lane is intentionally smaller than general software-engineering and language worlds.
statement: Provenance records who or what requested an operation, which capability authorized it, and which result followed.

label: Deterministic reducer
limitations: This custom lane is intentionally smaller than general software-engineering and language worlds.
statement: A reducer applies one event to one prior state to produce one next state without hidden side effects.

label: Requirement
limitations: This custom lane is intentionally smaller than general software-engineering and language worlds.
statement: A requirement states an observable obligation, constraint, exclusion, or quality target without prematurely choosing implementation structure.

label: Retry policy
limitations: This custom lane is intentionally smaller than general software-engineering and language worlds.
statement: A retry policy declares eligible failures, attempt limits, delay, jitter, and idempotency requirements.

label: Non-idempotent retry control
limitations: This custom lane is intentionally smaller than general software-engineering and language worlds.
statement: An effectful operation without deduplication must not be retried automatically as though repetition were harmless.

label: First-principles Rust orchestration
limitations: This custom lane is intentionally smaller than general software-engineering and language worlds.
statement: A Rust orchestrator decomposes requirements into typed state, messages, capabilities, workers, and explicit failure behavior before assembling an application.

label: Side-effect boundary
limitations: This custom lane is intentionally smaller than general software-engineering and language worlds.
statement: External writes and irreversible effects occur behind explicit interfaces that can be reviewed, tested, and substituted.

label: State machine
limitations: This custom lane is intentionally smaller than general software-engineering and language worlds.
statement: A state machine declares valid states, transitions, guards, and terminal conditions.

label: Stringly typed bus control
limitations: This custom lane is intentionally smaller than general software-engineering and language worlds.
statement: Ad-hoc message strings must not be treated as equivalent to a typed message contract.

label: Supervision
limitations: This custom lane is intentionally smaller than general software-engineering and language worlds.
statement: Supervision observes worker termination and applies a declared restart, isolate, escalate, or stop policy.

label: Timeout
limitations: This custom lane is intentionally smaller than general software-engineering and language worlds.
statement: A timeout bounds waiting and produces an explicit outcome; it does not prove the remote operation stopped.

label: Timeout-is-not-stop control
limitations: This custom lane is intentionally smaller than general software-engineering and language worlds.
statement: A timeout must not be reported as proof that an external operation terminated.

label: Unbounded-channel control
limitations: This custom lane is intentionally smaller than general software-engineering and language worlds.
statement: An unbounded channel must not be described as backpressure because producers can continue allocating without waiting for capacity.

label: Unit test
limitations: This custom lane is intentionally smaller than general software-engineering and language worlds.
statement: A unit test isolates a component law with controlled inputs and expected outcomes.

label: Worker
limitations: This custom lane is intentionally smaller than general software-engineering and language worlds.
statement: A worker owns execution of a narrow task contract and reports outcomes through typed events.
